En: His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing floor, gathering his wheat into the barn and burning up the chaff with unquenchable fire.
Ib: Ihe o ji je-ayọcha ihe ubie dị am na ẹka. Ya o jege na ibe o keye na-ayọcha a, na o weri nke bụ ezibe akpụrụ gbaa na ẹkpa pabaa na ọba, kpo[1]ru ndem bụ ẹhụrụ wụbaa na ọkụ aanyụhụgụ anyụhụ.”

En: The Baptism of Jesus
Ib: Omume Jisọs Baụtizim

En: Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John.
Ib: Jisọs hi na Galili bịa na ẹnyụm Jọdan na Jọn mie ye baụtizim.

En: But John tried to deter him, saying,
Ib: Jọn na-achọ na ọ kwụsị a, sị a,

En: “I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?”
Ib: “Ị bịarị na mụ emie gi baụtizim ibe ọ bụ mụoni kwesiri ịbịa na i mie m baụtizim?”

En: Jesus replied, “Let it be so now; it is proper for us to do this to fulfill all righteousness.”
Ib: Jisọs sị a, “Hasịa ya na ọ dị ya ẹɦụm ẹɦụọdị. Ọ dị ma na ayị mezue ọchụchọ Chineke na ohu.”

En: Then John consented.
Ib: Jọn kwezuu.

En: As soon as Jesus was baptized, he went up out of the water.
Ib: E mefurum Jisọs baụtizim, ya o hi na ime mini nyikote.

En: At that moment heaven was opened, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and alighting on him.
Ib: Elugwe kpuhee, ya ọ hụ Maa Nsọ ibe o hi na elugwe heride ka ẹkpala

En: And a voice from heaven said,
Ib: Olu hi na elugwe daa sị,

En: “This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased.”
Ib: “Onyie bụ Nwa m nwoke m hụrụ na ẹnya ọkam, ihie dịŋaarị m ma.”

En: Jesus Is Tested in the Wilderness
Ib: Ọnwụnwa A Nwarị Jisọs

En: Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.
Ib: Maa Nsọ duru Jisọs na-eje na ọzara, ibe o keyeri Ekwensu nwaa ya ọnwụnwa.

En: After fasting forty days and forty nights, he was hungry.
Ib: Mgbe Jisọs vuduru ọnụ na ekpere ihu abalị ẹbọọ, ehihe maa abalị, ezibe ẹgụ gidie.

En: The tempter came to him and said, “If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread.”
Ib: Ya onye ọnwụnwam bụ Ekwensu garị jekwute Jisọs bịa-asị a, “Ibe ị bụ ya Ọkparam nke Chineke, sị mkpumiega wo gọa buredi.”

En: Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.’ ”
Ib: Jisọs sị a, “E deri e na Ẹkwụkwọ Nsọ sị, ‘Madụ amagị e jinwe ọtịta buredi yaanịa dị ndụ, kama ọ bụ hite na okwu ọọbụla hi Chineke na ọnụ.’ ”

En: Then the devil took him to the holy city and had him stand on the highest point of the temple.
Ib: Ekwensu dukwekweri e na-eje alị nsọ Jerusalẹm, duru e nyikoru ibe kakọta na elu na Oke Ulo Nsọ, sị a,

En: “If you are the Son of God,” he said, “throw yourself down.
Ib: “Ibe ị bụ ya Ọkparam nke Chineke, hi na ibie tụda onwogu.

En: For it is written: “ ‘He will command his angels concerning you, and they will lift you up in their hands, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.’ ”
Ib: E deri e na Ẹkwụkwọ Nsọ sị,“ ‘Chineke je-anị ndemaaozi e iwu bayeri gi,na wo je-eji ẹka wo parị gị,na ị kpọbukwe ọkpa na mkpume.’ ”

En: Jesus answered him, “It is also written: ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’ ”
Ib: Jisọs sị a, “E dekoru e na Ẹkwụkwọ Nsọ sị, ‘Anwagile[1]kwe Onyenwoayị bụ Chineke gi ọnwụnwa.’ ”

En: Again, the devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their splendor.
Ib: Ekwensu dukwekweri e nyikoru ugwu aanị harị pagom na elu, je-egusikobie alịeze ụwa oohu dị iche iche, maa ẹkụ maa ọmọlọma wo oohu, sị a,

En: “All this I will give you,” he said, “if you will bow down and worship me.”
Ib: “Eje m anị gị ihie na ohu ị hụrụ ma gị kwe huride kpọarị m isi na alị.”

En: Jesus said to him, “Away from me, Satan!
Ib: Jisọs sị a, “Fụ m na ihu Ekwensu!

En: For it is written: ‘Worship the Lord your God, and serve him only.’ ”
Ib: E deri e na Ẹkwụkwọ Nsọ sị, ‘Ọ bụ Onyenwoayị bụ Chineke gi bụ onye ị je-ịkpọrụ isi na alị, jieri yaanịa ozi.’ ”

En: Then the devil left him, and angels came and attended him.
Ib: Ekwensu habuzue Jisọs garị na-asọhụ, nde maaozi bịa na-ejeri e ozi.

En: Jesus Begins to Preach
Ib: Jisọs Malite Ozi E

En: When Jesus heard that John had been put in prison, he withdrew to Galilee.
Ib: Mgbe Jisọs nụrụ na e gidewo Jọn ome baụtizim je-atụ mkpọrọ, ya ọ garị galata na Galili.

En: Leaving Nazareth, he went and lived in Capernaum, which was by the lake in the area of Zebulun and Naphtali—to fulfill what was said through the prophet Isaiah:
Ib: Jisọs habue Nazarẹtị garị laga Kapanọm je-eburu. Kapanọm dị na agịga ẹnyụm dị na ọnụmara Zebulọn yaa Naftalị. Ọ bụ nke a garị ihe onye amụma Ayịzaya kwuru mezue, sịnị,

En: “Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles—
Ib: “Alị Zebulọn yaa alị Naftalị, dị na ụzọ ma a kpọdaje ẹnyụm, na ndabu Jọdan,na Galili alị nde aabụgụ nde Juu na-ebuko,

En: the people living in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death a light has dawned.”
Ib: ndem bụ nde buru na ẹtụlị, ahụwo oke ihe. Ndem buweeri na alị nke onyunyo ọnwụ, ihe achakwasịwo wo.”

En: From that time on Jesus began to preach,
Ib: Hite na ya mgbem, Jisọs malite na-ezise oziọma sị wo,

En: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.”
Ib: “Unu chegeridue habue ụmara ọjọọ uunu maka na Alịeze Elugwe dịzunwe nso.”

En: Jesus Calls His First Disciples
Ib: Jisọs Họta Nde Na-eso Ụzọ Mbụ A

En: As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew.
Ib: Mgbe Jisọs gajejeri na akwa ẹnyụm Galili, ya ọ hụ ụmụne ndikom ẹbọọ, Saịmọn a na-eku Pita yaa nwanie nwoke Anduru.

En: They were casting a net into the lake, for they were fishermen.
Ib: Wo nọrụ na-ese ụgbụ maka na wo bụrụ nde ọkụ ụba.

En: “Come, follow me,” Jesus said, “and I will send you out to fish for people.”
Ib: Jisọs sị wo, “Unu so m, eje m je-eme unu nde ọkụ na-akụta madụ.”

En: At once they left their nets and followed him.
Ib: Wo nọm na ya mgbem wụsị ụgbụ wo maa ntofo wo, pavuru so Jisọs.

En: Going on from there, he saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John.
Ib: Ya o hi na ya ibom zọhụbatụ[1]rụ, ya ọ hụkwakwa ụmụne ndikom ẹbọọ ọzọ, Jems yaa Jọn, ụmụ Zebedii.

En: They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, preparing their nets.
Ib: Woa nna wo Zebedii nọrụ na ụgbọ na-emeche ụgbụ wo.

En: Jesus called them,and immediately they left the boat and their father and followed him.
Ib: Jisọs sị wo so e. Wo nọm na ya mgbem habue nna wo maa ụgbọ wo, pavuru so Jisọs.

En: Jesus Heals the Sick
Ib: Jisọs Gwọa Nde Ụhụka

En: Jesus went throughout Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness among the people.
Ib: Jisọs na-agakọba Galili na ohu, na-ezi ihe na ulo-ozuzu woga, na-ezise Oziọma bayeri Alịeze Elugwe, na-agwọ nde ụhụka nọrụ na etiti wo.

En: News about him spread all over Syria, and people brought to him all who were ill with various diseases, those suffering severe pain, the demon-possessed, those having seizures, and the paralyzed; and he healed them.
Ib: Ude Jisọs deserehi na alị Siria na ohu. Nde madụ na-ekuteri e nde ụhụka wo dịgarị iche iche, maa nde maaọ-jọọ jigeri, nde ndakwụkwụ maa nde ẹnwụmaa, Jisọs na-agwọ wo.

En: Large crowds from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea and the region across the Jordan followed him.
Ib: Ntụtụ madụ hiri na Galili maa na isi ogo iri a na-eku Dekapolis, maa Jerusalẹm, maa Judia, maa nde higeri na ndabu ẹnyụm Jọdan, bịa-esoru Jisọs.

En: Introduction to the Sermon on the Mount
Ib: Ozi E Keyeri Na Elu Ugwu Zie

En: Now when Jesus saw the crowds, he went up on a mountainside and sat down.
Ib: Mgbe Jisọs hụrụ ntụtụ madụ gbakọtarị, ya ọ garị nyikoru na elu ugwu aanị je-anọdụa ọdụ.

En: His disciples came to him, and he began to teach them.
Ib: Nde na-eso ụzọ a garị bịakwute e.

En: The Beatitudes
Ib: Ozizi Bayeri Nde Nwo Ezibe Obu-ụtọ

En: He said:“Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Ib: Jisọs malite na-ezi wo ihe sị, Ngọzi dịịrị ndem maarịna wo enwogu ihe nke ime maa,maka na Alịeze Elugwe bụ nke wo.

En: Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.
Ib: Ngọzi dịịrị ndem nọ na erim-ụjụ, maka na a je-akasi wo obu.

En: Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.
Ib: Ngọzi dịịrị ndem na-eweride onwowo alị,maka na wo je-eri elụwa na ekpe.

En: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.
Ib: Ngọzi dịịrị ndem ọ na-ọgụŋarị ẹgụ ime ụmara-ọma, maka na e je-eme na wo ahụ ihe wo chọrụ.

En: Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.
Ib: Ngọzi dịịrị ndem na-ahụ nde ọzọ onyimee, maka na a je-ahụkọ woande onyimee.

En: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
Ib: Ngọzi dịịrị ndem obu wo dị ọcha,maka na wo je-ahụ Chineke ẹnya.

En: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
Ib: Ngọzi dịịrị ndem na-ekpe udo, maka na a je-eku wo ụmụ Chineke.

En: Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Ib: Ngọzi dịịrị ndem nde madụ na emegide maka na wo na-eme ụmara-ọma,maka na Alịeze Elugwe bụ nke wo.

En: “Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of me.
Ib: Ngọzi dịịrị gị mgbem nde madụ na-akparị gị, na-emegide gi, na-agabo gu ụga ihe ọjọọ dị iche iche maka na ị tụkwasịrị m obu.

En: Rejoice and be glad, because great is your reward in heaven, for in the same way they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
Ib: Nwụrịa ọnwụ, na obu-ụtọ dị gị maka na ụgwọ-ọrụ gụ na ihu Chineke kpọrụ ẹdụm. Ọ bụ nke nde madụ megidegeri nde amụmam buru unu ụzọ bịa.

En: Salt and Light
Ib: Ozizi Maka Unu Yaa Ihe

En: “You are the salt of the earth.
Ib: Unu bụ unu nke elụwa.

En: But if the salt loses its saltiness, how can it be made salty again?
Ib: Ọbụ naa unu hasịa ihe o jiri bụrụ unu, atọsịgị unu unu, e ji gịnị je-emekwekwe e na ọ bụrụ unu?

En: It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled underfoot.
Ib: Ọ dịsịgị ihe ọ dịkwa ma iji e me katakwa iweri e wụfụ ezi, na nde madụ azọtọsịa ya na ọkpa.

En: “You are the light of the world.
Ib: “Unu bụ ihe nke ụwa.

En: A town built on a hill cannot be hidden.
Ib: Obodo e wuru na mgbakwasịrị ugwu enwogu ezomi.

En: Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a bowl.
Ib: Ọ dịkwanụgụ onye na-amụye oriọkụ pabaa na okpuru ihe.

En: Instead they put it on its stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house.
Ib: Kama a na-ọdọbaje oriọkụ na elu ihe ma onye ọọbụla nọ na ulo weri e hụje ụzọ.

En: In the same way, let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.
Ib: Unu mee na ihe uunu chawaa na ihu ụmụ madụ, na wo jiri e hụta ọrụ ọma uunu, toe Nnade uunu bu na elugwe.

En: The Fulfillment of the Law
Ib: Ozizi Maka Iwu Mosisi

En: “Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets;
Ib: “Unu arịkwa na-abịarị m ịkagbu iwu Mosisi ma ọ bụgụ ihe nde amụma kwugeri.

En: I have not come to abolish them but to fulfill them.
Ib: Waa, abịadịgị m wo akagbu, kama a bịarị m imezutum wo oohu.

En: For truly I tell you, until heaven and earth disappear, not the smallest letter, not the least stroke of a pen, will by any means disappear from the Law until everything is accomplished.
Ib: Na nke bụ eziokwu, tututu na elugwe yaa elụwa agabuge, ọ dịgị ma akpụrụ ẹkwụkwọm kadụa ahaba ẹka, ma ọ bụgụ akara edemedem ka[1]dụa ẹka ahaba sọhụ na Iwu Mosisi tututu na-emezutuem ihe e deri na ya.

En: Therefore anyone who sets aside one of the least of these commands and teaches others accordingly will be called least in the kingdom of heaven,
Ib: Onye ọọbụla mebiri ọmụ kadụa ẹka ahaba na ya iwuega, na-eziko nde ọzọ wo mebijeko iwu, je-abụ onye e kuru onye kadụa ẹka ahaba na Alịeze Elugwe.

En: but whoever practices and teaches these commands will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
Ib: Ọbụ na onye ọọbụla na erube isi na ibe iwu Mosisi dị, na-eziko nde ọzọ wo rubejekoru e isi je-abụ onye e kuru ẹkpọtọlọ na Alịeze Elugwe.

En: For I tell you that unless your righteousness surpasses that of the Pharisees and the teachers of the law, you will certainly not enter the kingdom of heaven.
Ib: Maka na-asị m unu, ọ bụkwam ma ụmara-ọma uunu ọ karịrị nke nde Farisii woa nde na-ezi iwu Mosisi, ọ dịgị nke unu je-aga gabaa Alịeze Elugwe.

En: Murder
Ib: Ozizi Maka Iwe

En: “You have heard that it was said to the people long ago, ‘You shall not murder, and anyone who murders will be subject to judgment.’
Ib: “Unu anụwo na a sịrị nde mgbe ichie, ‘Egbukwe madụ, onye ọọbụla gburu madụ na-ekpie ye ikpe.’

En: But I tell you that anyone who is angry with a brother or sister will be subject to judgment.
Ib: Ọbụ na-asị m unu, onye ọọbụla weeri nwanie iwe na-ekpie ye ikpe.

En: Again, anyone who says to a brother or sister, ‘Raca ,’ is answerable to the court.
Ib: Ọzọkwa bụ, onye ọọbụla sịrị nwanie, ‘Raka’d na-akpụfụta a na ihu nde ichie.

En: And anyone who says, ‘You fool!’ will be in danger of the fire of hell.
Ib: Ọbụ na onye sịrị madụ, ‘Gịa onye iberibie’ nọ na ntaram-ahụhụ ọkụmaa aanyụhụgụ anyụhụ.

En: “Therefore, if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother or sister has something against you,
Ib: “Ọ bụ a meri onye jiri ihe ọnịnị jije na ihu Chineke rịta na o nworu nwanie o meri ihe aadịgị ma,

En: leave your gift there in front of the altar.
Ib: onye ọ bụ je-ahabu ihe ọnịnị a na ihu ekwuẹjae,

En: First go and be reconciled to them; then come and offer your gift.
Ib: jekwuhee nwanie ọ bụ na yaa ya ekpezie, ta na ọ bịataje ọchụchụ ẹja a na ihu Chineke.

En: “Settle matters quickly with your adversary who is taking you to court.
Ib: “Onye yaa madụ nwoteeri esemokwu hụụ na wo kpeziri hoohoo, na wo akpụfụkwa a na ulo ikpe.

En: Do it while you are still together on the way, or your adversary may hand you over to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and you may be thrown into prison.
Ib: Na ọ bụ ya o kwe wo dufu e na ulo ikpe, na ọkikpe wo eweri e ye na ẹka nde ọchịmkpọrọ, na wo eweri e dubee na mkpọrọ.

En: Truly I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the last penny.
Ib: Na eziokwu a sị m unu, ọ dịgị ma wo kwie hii na ya ulo mkpọrọm fụta tututu na ọ kwụtuem ihe wo boru e, ọ dịgị ma ọ kwụhọ ma ọ bụgụ afụ.

En: Adultery
Ib: Ozizi Maka Mmeko Nwoke Yaa Nwanyị Aalụtaarịgị Onwowo

En: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall not commit adultery.’
Ib: “Unu nụrụ na a sị, ‘Onye ejekwe na nwanyị aabụgụ nyee ye.’

En: But I tell you that anyone who looks at a woman lustfully has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
Ib: Ọbụ na mụ aakarị unu, onye ọọbụla lekoheerinwe nwanyị ọzọ aabụgụ nyee ye ẹnya, ya ọ gụa ya na yaa ya nwoe mmeko, ejekoduwori na nwanyị ọ bụ na ime obu e.

En: If your right eye causes you to stumble, gouge it out and throw it away.
Ib: Ya ọ bụrụ na ẹnya ikenge gi je-evuteri gi omume ihe ọjọọ, kpafụta a lọhue.

En: It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to be thrown into hell.
Ib: Ọ kaarị gị ma na i lọhuru ẹkụkụ ụhụ gụ aanị kama a je-atụba ụhụ gụ oohu na ọkụmaa.

En: And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away.
Ib: Ya ọ bụkwanụrụ ẹka ikenge gi je-edube gi na omume ihe ọjọọ, gbufu e lọhue.

En: It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to go into hell.
Ib: Ọ kaarị gị ma na ị lọhuru ẹkụkụ ụhụ gụ aanị kama a je-atụba ụhụ gụ oohu na ọkụmaa.

En: Divorce
Ib: Ozizi Maka Achụfụ Nyee Madụ Na Ọ Lụsịgị A

En: “It has been said, ‘Anyone who divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.’
Ib: “A sịkọrụ, ‘Onye lụtụ nwanyị achọsịgị a ọlụlụ, ya ọ chụfụ a, kpekeyie ẹkwụkwọ na-egusi na ọ lụsịgị a.’

En: But I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, makes her the victim of adultery, and anyone who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
Ib: Ọbụ na-asị m unu, onye ọọbụla chụfụrụ nyee ye, kpahakwaa na o gideri e yaa nwoke ọzọ, na-edube nyee ye na-ọgbụgba ọkwa. Onye ọọbụla jekwenuru jealụta nwanyị di e chụfụrụ na-eje na nyee onye ọzọ.

En: Oaths
Ib: Ozizi Maka Ọnwụnwụ Ihe

En: “Again, you have heard that it was said to the people long ago, ‘Do not break your oath, but fulfill to the Lord the vows you have made.’
Ib: “Ọzọkwakwa, unu nụrụ na e kwuuru nnade oche uunu sị wo, ‘Onye anwụkwa ihe, kwe nkwa ihe ọ maarị na o jegi je-eme eme, kama onyeaha mezue nkwa o keyeri na ihu Chineke kwe.’

En: But I tell you, do not swear an oath at all:
Ib: Ọbụ na-asị m unu, onye anwụkwam ihe anwụ na ohu.

En: either by heaven, for it is God’s throne;or by the earth, for it is his footstool; or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the Great King.
Ib: Ejikwe elugwe nwụa ihe maka na ọ. Atakwarị madụ alị, ma ọ bụgụ jiri elụwa nwụa ihe maka na ọ bụ ibe awụkwasị ọkpa Chineke, jikwenugu Jerusalẹm nwụa ihe, maka na ọ bụ alị ya oke Ezem.

En: And do not swear by your head, for you cannot make even one hair white or black.
Ib: Onye ejikwe isi e nwụa ihe, maka na ọ dịgị onye nworu ike ime ẹgbịsị isi e aanị na o due ndu ma ọ bụgụ chaa ụcha.

En: All you need to say is simply ‘Yes’ or ‘No’; anything beyond this comes from the evil one.
Ib: Kama onye ọọbụla je-ekwu okwu, na, ‘Ẹẹ’ bụrụ ‘Ẹẹ’ na, ‘Waa’ bụrụ ‘Waa.’ Ya ọ gatam ya ẹɦụm, o hizu na ẹka ya onye ọjọọm.

En: Eye for Eye
Ib: Ozizi Maka Emewete Ihe

En: “You have heard that it was said, ‘Eye for eye, and tooth for tooth.’
Ib: “Unu nụworu na a sịrị, ‘Onye dụpịa madụ ẹnya aanị, a dụpịakọ a ẹnya aanị, onye kụfụ madụ akpụrụ eze aanị, akụfụkọ a akpụrụ eze aanị.’

En: But I tell you, do not resist an evil person.
Ib: Ọbụ na-asị m unu, na ọ dịkwa mgbe unu je-eje agwata onye meri unu ihe ọjọọ imeri.

En: If anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to them the other cheek also.
Ib: Onye jụ gụ ẹka na ntie, tụgarịfụrụ a ọmụ mbụ nti na ọ jụfụrụ.

En: And if anyone wants to sue you and take your shirt, hand over your coat as well.
Ib: Madụ kufu gu na ulo ikpe je na-azọ uwe gi i ye, chịtakọrị uwe i ye na ime ụhụ gụ yekoru e.

En: If anyone forces you to go one mile, go with them two miles.
Ib: Onye kwogide gi na ikike na i je-iso e jie ije maịnị aanị, soru e jie maịnị ẹbọọ.

En: Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you.
Ib: Onye rịarị gị ihe wetee nị a, anọmbekwe jụka onye bịarị gị agbanata nzi.

En: Love for Enemies
Ib: Ozizi Maka Ịhụ Nde-iro Gu Na Ẹnya

En: “You have heard that it was said, ‘Love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’
Ib: “Unu nụworu na a sị, ‘Hụ onye ndịma gị na ẹnya, ahụkwa onye-iro gu na ẹnya.’

En: But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, that you may be children of your Father in heaven.
Ib: Ọbụ na-asị m, hụ nde-iro gu na ẹnya! Kpejeri nde naakpagbu gu ekpere. Unu na-eme ya ẹɦụm, na unu abụrụ ụmụ Nnade uunu nọ na elugwe.

En: He causes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.
Ib: Ọ bụ a na-eme anwụ na-etiri nde ọma maa nde ihe ọjọọ. Na-eme mini na-ezoru nde ụmara-ọma maa nde ụmara-ọjọọ.

En: If you love those who love you, what reward will you get?
Ib: Unu na-ahụnwa nde hụrụ unu na ẹnya, ndaa ụgwọ-ọrụ dịịrị unu?

En: Are not even the tax collectors doing that?
Ib: Ọ bụ na nde na-anarị nde Rom ụtụ takịsị emekogegi ya ẹɦụm?

En: And if you greet only your own people, what are you doing more than others?
Ib: Ya ọ bụrụ nwa ụmụne uunu bụ nde unu kweri ihe wo, ndaa ihe unu na-eme nde ọzọ eemekogegi?

En: Do not even pagans do that?
Ib: Ọ bụ na nde mba ọzọ aamagị Chineke emekogegi ya ẹɦụm?

En: Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
Ib: Ọ bụ a meri, unu je-ezuriri oke na ụmara-ọma ẹɦụm Nnade uunu nọ na elugwe zuru oke.

En: Giving to the Needy
Ib: Ozizi Maka Ịnị Ndem Ọọdịgị Nke Ọha Wo Ihe

En: “Be careful not to practice your righteousness in front of others to be seen by them.
Ib: “Unu hụụ na unu emegi ụmara-ọma uunu na ihu ọha ma wo hụ unu, jaa unu ike.

En: If you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.
Ib: Unu me ya ẹɦụm ka Nnade uunu nọ na elugwe aakwụsị unu ụgwọ-ọrụ.

En: “So when you give to the needy, do not announce it with trumpets, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets, to be honored by others.
Ib: “Unu je-anị nde ọọdịgị nke ọha wo ihe, unu ahụkwa ofuike zie ọha ihe unu je-omume. Dịka nde mma ihu ẹbọọ na-eje na ulo-ozuzu, gakọba ibeaha na ohu ma nde madụ hụ ihe wo meri naje wo ẹka.

En: Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.
Ib: Ana m ekwuru unu nke bụ eziokwu, wo anatatuwori ụgwọ-ọrụ wo.

En: But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,so that your giving may be in secret.
Ib: Ọbụ, unu je je-aanị nde ọọdịgị nke ọha wo ihe, unu ekwekwe na ẹka ibite uunu makọhaarị ihe ẹka ikenge uunu na-eme. Unu mie yeri na ezomi.

En: Then your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
Ib: Na Nnade uunu na-ahụtum ihe e megeri na ezomi je-akwụhachi unu ụgwọ-ọrụ.”

En: Prayer
Ib: Ozizi Bayeri Ekpere

En: “And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen by others.
Ib: “Unu je je-ekpe ekpere, unu adịkwa ka nde mma ihu ẹbọọ. Wo na-achọje na wo je je-eguzo na ulo-ozuzu, maa na ẹkụkụ ụzọga, ibe nde madụ je-ahụ wo na wo na-ekpe ekpere.

En: Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.
Ib: Ana m ekwuru unu nke bụ eziokwu, wo anatatuwori ụgwọ-ọrụ wo oohu.

En: But when you pray, go into your room, close the door and pray to your Father, who is unseen.
Ib: Ọbụ unu je je-ekpe ekpere, unu gabaa, je[1]agụchibudo onwuunu ulo, kpieri Nnade uunu nọrị na ibe zoru ezo.

En: Then your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
Ib: Na Nnade uunu na-ahụtum ihe emegeri maa na ezomi akwụhachi unu ụgwọ-ọrụ.

En: And when you pray, do not keep on babbling like pagans, for they think they will be heard because of their many words.
Ib: “Mgbe unu na-ekpekwenu ekpere, unu anọsị na-agụjasị agba ka nde mba ọzọ aamagị Chineke. Maka na wo na-arịị na ọ bụ wo kwue ntụtụ okwu na-anụ ekpere wo.

En: Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
Ib: Unu emekwe ka wo, maka na Nnade uunu amatuworuri ihe bụ mkpa uunu mgbe unu aaka arịakọhaagị a.

En: “This, then, is how you should pray:
Ib: “Ịhụ nke unu je-aga na-ekpe ekpere,

En: “Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
Ib: “ ‘Nnade ayị nọ na elugwe, na-asọfụrụ ẹha nsọ gụ, na ọchịchị gị bịa, na-emie uche gi na ụwa ẹɦụm e na-emie na elugwe.

En: Give us today our daily bread.
Ib: Nị ayị nri je-ezuru ayị nke izuha.

En: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
Ib: Gbaharị ayị ihe ọjọọ na ohu ayị meri gi,ẹɦụm ayị na-agbahakọrụ nde na-eme ayị ihe ọjọọ.

En: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. ’
Ib: Ekwekwe na ayị dabaa na ime ọnwụnwa, kama nafụta ayị na ẹka ya onye ọjọọm.’

En: For if you forgive other people when they sin against you, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
Ib: Maka mgbe unu gbahaarị nde madụ ihe ọjọọ wo meri unu, na Nnade uunu nọ na elugwe agbaharị unu nke uunu mbụ ihe ọjọọ.

En: But if you do not forgive others their sins, your Father will not forgive your sins.
Ib: Mgbe unu aagbahaarịgị nde madụ ihe ọjọọ wo meri unu, ka Nnade uunu nọ na elugwe aagbahakọrụ unu ihe ọjọọ uunu.”

En: Fasting
Ib: Ozizi Maka Ovuvu Ọnụ

En: “When you fast, do not look somber as the hypocrites do, for they disfigure their faces to show others they are fasting.
Ib: “Unu je-evu ọnụ, unu eje ewesiri ihu uunu gbanwụbadụa ka nde mma ihu ẹbọọ. Wo na-eweri ihu wo gbanwụbadụa ma nde madụ hụ wo marị na wo na-evu ọnụ.

En: Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.
Ib: Na eziokwu, wo anatatuwori ụgwọ-ọrụ wo.

En: But when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face,
Ib: Ọbụ unu je-evu ọnụ, unu kwọchaa ihu uunu, wete manụ hue na isi uunu.

En: so that it will not be obvious to others that you are fasting, but only to your Father, who is unseen; and your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
Ib: Na ọ bụkwa na ẹnya nde madụ bụ ibe unu je-abụ nde na-evu ọnụ, kama na Nnade uunu nọ na elugwe aahụgụ ẹnya, na-ahụtum ihe emegeri maa na ezomi kwụhachi unu ụgwọ-ọrụ.

En: Treasures in Heaven
Ib: Ozizi Maka Akpado Ẹkụ Na Elugwe

En: “Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moths and vermin destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.
Ib: “Unu akpadosiri onwuunu ẹkụ na elụwa, ibe ụtụ na-agba ma ọ bụgụ na ọ taa nkarafọ, na nde ohi ana-akụwasị ibeaha na-ezu.

En: But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where moths and vermin do not destroy, and where thieves do not break in and steal.
Ib: Kama unu kpadoru onwuunu ẹkụ na elugwe, ibe ụtụ eemebisigi madụ ihe, ka ọọta nkarafọ, ka nde ohi aagbaka ulo zue ohi.

En: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
Ib: Maka na ọ bụ ibe ẹkụ madụ dị bụkọ ibe obu e je-adị.

En: “The eye is the lamp of the body.
Ib: “Ẹnya dịka oriọkụ na-eweteri madụ ihe na ụhụ a.

En: If your eyes are healthy, your whole body will be full of light.
Ib: Ya ọ bụrụ na ẹnya gị ana-ahụcha ụzọ, na ihe eju gụ ụhụ na ohu.

En: But if your eyes are unhealthy, your whole body will be full of darkness.
Ib: Ọbụ na ya ọ bụrụ na o nworu ihe meri gi na ẹnya, na ị marị na ụhụ gụ na ohu je-anọ na ẹtụlị.

En: If then the light within you is darkness, how great is that darkness!
Ib: Ya ọ bụrụ na ihe dị gị na ụhụ abụrụ ẹtụlị, ọ je ọ bụ ezibe oke ẹtụlị!

En: “No one can serve two masters.
Ib: “Ọ dịgị onye je-enwochete nnadukwu ẹbọọ na akpa aanị.

En: Either you will hate the one and love the other, or you will be devoted to the one and despise the other.
Ib: Maka na onye ọ bụ je-ekweriri ihe nnanị ka ookweihe ọmụanịm, ma ọ bụgụ na o na-ojecheri nnanị ozi na-eleli nnanịm ẹnya.

En: You cannot serve both God and money.
Ib: Ọ dịgị madụ je-emechete Chineke yaa ẹkụ na ụba nnịa ukwu na akpa aanị.

En: “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear.
Ib: “Ọ bụ a meri m sị unu, onye adọgbusi onwoe bayeri ndụ a, bayeri ihe o je-ori yaa ihe ọ je-ọnwụ. Maa ọ bụgụ bayeri ụhụ a, ihe o je-oji yechie ụhụ a.

En: Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?
Ib: Ọ bụ na ndụ akarịgị nri e ji na-azụ a, saa ụhụ ọ karịgị ihe e ji na-eyechi e?

En: Look at the birds of the air; they do not sow or reap or store away in barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them.
Ib: Unu letekwele nnụnụ na-ehegerige na elu. Ọ dịgị ibe wo kọyeri ubi, dịgị ọba wo deberi wo na-edebe ihe wo gọtarị na ubi, ọbụ na Nnade uunu nọ na elugwe na-azụ wo nri.

En: Are you not much more valuable than they?
Ib: Ọ bụ na unu akagị wo mkpa?

En: Can any one of you by worrying add a single hour to your life ?
Ib: Ndaa onye na ime uunu hite na-adọgbu onwoe nworu ike igbayeko ma ọ bụgụ abalị aanị na ndụ a?

En: “And why do you worry about clothes?
Ib: “Ndaa ihe merini unu na[1]adọgbu onwuunu maka ẹkụ oyiye?

En: See how the flowers of the field grow.
Ib: Unu letekwele ẹwụwụ dịga na ọhịa nke wo na-eso,

En: They do not labor or spin.
Ib: wo adọgbugu onwowo na ọrụ na-ekwo ẹkụ wo je-eye.

En: Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his splendor was dressed like one of these.
Ib: Ọbụ na Solomọnụ na nkwọkọ a na ohu maa ẹkụ a amakwudigi nnanị na ime wo na mma.

En: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the fire, will he not much more clothe you—you of little faith?
Ib: Ibe Chineke na eyechige ya ẹwụwụ aga bụ gị hụdụa yanwa taa, echi na-asụsịa ya wụbaa na ọkụ, ndaa nke oomogoyechi unuande? E meri ẹgaa okwukwe uunu ha tịkọọ?

En: So do not worry, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’
Ib: Unu anọsị na-adọgbu onwuunu na-asị, ‘Ndaa ihe ayị je-eri?’ ma ọ bụgụ, ‘Ndaa ihe ayị je-anwụ?’ ma ọ bụgụ, ‘Ndaa ihe ayị je-eye?’

En: For the pagans run after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them.
Ib: Maka na nde mba ọzọ aamagị Chineke bụ ihe wo na-adọgbu onwowo na-achọ. Nnade uunu nọ na elugwe amaduworu na ya ihie na ohu dị unu mkpa.

En: But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.
Ib: Kama unu buru ụzọ chọa Alịeze Chineke, yaa ụmara-ọma a, na ihe nde ọzọm na ohu abụzurunwe ịkpa ẹka nịa unu.

En: 34 Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own.
Ib: 34.   Ọ bụ a meri, unu adọgbukosi onwuunu bayeri ihe je-agba echi, maka na echi je-akpa ụka onwoe, unu ejisi ẹka uunu na-eweteyekoru onwuunu mmekesi ụhụ.

En: Judging Others
Ib: Ozizi Maka Ikpe Nde Ọzọ Ikpe

En: “Do not judge, or you too will be judged.
Ib: “Ekpekwe nde ọzọ ikpe na e kpekokwe gịoni.

En: For in the same way you judge others, you will be judged, and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you.
Ib: Maka na ọ bụ ẹka-ikpe ị tọyeeri onye ọzọ bụ ẹka-ikpe a je-atọyeri gi, ntụtụ i jiri tụarị onye ọzọ bụ ihe e je-eji tụarị gị.

En: “Why do you look at the speck of sawdust in your brother’s eye and pay no attention to the plank in your own eye?
Ib: “E meri ẹgaa ị na-ịhụ ẹhịhịara ngwọ dị nwane gi na ẹnya ta ka ịịhụ okpirikpi nkụ zetooru gịoni na ẹnya?

En: How can you say to your brother, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye,’ when all the time there is a plank in your own eye?
Ib: Ị ga ẹgaa je-asị nwane gi, ‘Bịa na mụ aahụfụ gụ ẹhịhịara ngwọ dị gị na ẹnya,’ ibe okpirikpi nkụ zetokwenuuru gịoni na ẹnya.

En: You hypocrite, first take the plank out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.
Ib: Gịa onye mma ihu ẹbọọnwa, buru ụzọ je-apalahịhaa okpirikpi nkụm zetooru gu na ẹnya ma ị hụchaa ụzọ welehi nwane gi ẹhịhịara ngwọ dị a na ẹnya.

En: “Do not give dogs what is sacred; do not throw your pearls to pigs. If you do, they may trample them under their feet, and turn and tear you to pieces.
Ib: “Ewesiri ihe dị nsọ tụfụrụ nkịta , ma ọ bụgụ weri ihe baarị gị uru darị oke ọnụ ahịa tụfụrụ ezi. Wo je-azọtọsị a na ọkpa tụgarịkwaarị na-alụso gu ọgụ.

En: Ask, Seek, Knock
Ib: Rịa, Chọa, Kụa Ẹka

En: “Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and the door will be opened to you.
Ib: “Rịa ihe ị chọrụ na a je-anị gị a, chọa na ị je-ịchọta, kụa ẹka na ụkpụkpanị a je-emeheri gi.

En: For everyone who asks receives; the one who seeks finds; and to the one who knocks, the door will be opened.
Ib: Onye ọọbụla rịarịnị, a je-anị a ihe ọ rịarị, onye chọrụ ihe je-achọta, onye kụrụ ẹka na ụkpụkpanị na e meheeri e.

En: “Which of you, if your son asks for bread, will give him a stone?
Ib: Ndaa onye na ime uunu nde bụ nna, nwa a je-abịa bịa arịa buredi na ọ pata mkpume payie?

En: Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake?
Ib: Ma ọ bụgụ nwa a je-asị ya ọ nị a ụba na ọ chịta agwọ chịyie na ẹka?

En: If you, then, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good gifts to those who ask him!
Ib: Ibe unuande bụ madụ, ihe ọjọọ juru ime maarị nke a ga na-anị ụmụ uunu ihe dị ma, ndazukwenue nke Nnade uunu onye nọ na elugwe aamagị anị nde rịarịanị ihe dị ma!

En: So in everything, do to others what you would have them do to you, for this sums up the Law and the Prophets.
Ib: Ọ bụ a meri, gị marị ihe nde madụ je-eme gi na ọ dị gị ma, mieri nde ọzọ. Ọ bụ a bụ nchịkọta iwu Mosisi na ohu maa ihe nde amụma kwuru.

En: The Narrow and Wide Gates
Ib: Ọnụ Ụzọ Dị Mkpamkpa Yaa Nke Sarị Asa

En: “Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.
Ib: “Unu ga ọnụ ụzọm dị mkpamkpa gabaa, maka na ọnụ ụzọm sarị asa, ụzọ a dịa gbọọrịị na-edubee na alam-na-iyi, ntụtụ madụ na-agakwanụ a.

En: But small is the gate and narrow the road that leads to life, and only a few find it.
Ib: Ọbụ na ọnụ ụzọm hanwa wagụụ, ụzọ a siko ike bụ nke na-edubee na ndụ agwụ-agwụ, ọ dịkwanụnwa akpụ[1]rụ madụ ole na-achọvụta a.

En: True and False Prophets
Ib: Osisi Yaa Akpụrụ Ọ Mịrị

En: “Watch out for false prophets. They come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ferocious wolves.
Ib: “Unu kpacharị ẹnya maka nde amụma ụga. Wo na-emebenwe ka wo bụ atụrụ na elu ụhụ, ọbụ na ime wo, na wo abụrụ agụ owuru.

En: By their fruit you will recognize them. Do people pick grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
Ib: Unu ma amata wo hite na ihe wo na-emege. Ọ dị onye na-eje na ọhịa obiogwu je-agọta akpụrụ ụkpụkpa ma ọ bụgụ ọchịgịcha?

En: Likewise, every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit.
Ib: Ezibe osisi ọọbụla je-amị ezibe akpụrụ; na osisi ọjọọ amịa akpụrụ ọjọọ.

En: A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit.
Ib: Ezibe osisi amagị amị akpụrụ ọjọọ, dịkọkwanụgụ ma osisi ọjọọ mịa ezibe akpụrụ.

En: Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
Ib: Osisi ọọbụla aamịgị akpụrụ ọma, a je-egbutu e kpọa ọkụ.

En: Thus, by their fruit you will recognize them.
Ib: Nke bụanị bụ na unu je-amata ya nde amụma ụgam hite na ihe wo na-emege.

En: “Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.
Ib: “Ọ bụgụ madụ oohu na-asị m ‘Onyenwoayị, Onyenwoayị,’ je-agaba na Alịeze Elugwe, kama ọ bụ onye ọọbụla na-eme ihe Nna m nọ na elugwe chọrụ.

En: Many will say to me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name and in your name drive out demons and in your name perform many miracles?’Then I will tell them plainly, ‘I never knew you. Away from me, you evildoers!’
Ib: Na ya izukum, ntụtụ madụ je-asị m, ‘Onyenwoayị, Onyenwoayị, ọkwaa na ayị jiri ẹha gị na-evu amụma, na-achụfụkọga maaọjọọ jigeri nde madụ, rụkọgadụa ntụtụ ọrụ ebube na ẹha gị?’ 23Ya mgbem na mụ asị wo, ‘Ọ dịgị mgbe m mmaarị nde unu bụ; fụ m na ihu unuande ọrụ ihe ọjọọnwa!’

En: The Wise and Foolish Builders
Ib: Ụzọ Ntọalị Ẹbọọ

En: “Therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and puts them into practice is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.
Ib: “Onye ọọbụla nụrụ ihie m na-ekwu tiyie na ọrụ dịka onye maarị ihe jeri owuwu ulo e, je-ewukwesi e na elu mkpume.

En: The rain came down, the streams rose, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, because it had its foundation on the rock.
Ib: Mgbe mini ozuzo bịarị, oke okpukpo mini na-ekpo, ihuhe pavuru bịa-akwaŋaa ya ulom ta ka ọ da, maka na a tọrụ ntọalị ya ulom na elu oke mkpume.

En: But everyone who hears these words of mine and does not put them into practice is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.
Ib: Ọbụ na onye nụrụ ihie m na-ekwu ta ka o mie eme dịka onye iberibe jeri owuwu ulo e, je-eweri enwe wukwesi na elu nvọẹja.

En: The rain came down, the streams rose, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell with a great crash.”
Ib: Mgbe mini bịarị bịa-ezoe, okpukpo mini bido, ihuhe pavuru bịa-akwaŋaa ya ulom, ya o kwe gbirigidi, kụa pịagapịaga.”

En: When Jesus had finished saying these things, the crowds were amazed at his teaching,
Ib: Mgbe Jisọs kwuduru ya ihie na ohu, ndem na ohu nụrụ ihe o ziri wo gbatụ na ẹka, ya o ju wo ẹnya.

En: because he taught as one who had authority, and not as their teachers of the law.
Ib: Maka na Jisọs ziri wo ihe ka onye ihe docheri ẹnya, ọ bụgụ ka nde ozizi iwu Mosisi.

En: When Jesus came down from the mountainside, large crowds followed him.
Ib: Mgbe Jisọs hi na ya elu ugwum kpọride, ntụtụ madụ sochie ye azụ.

En: A man with leprosy came and knelt before him and said, “Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean.”
Ib: Nwoke aanị ụhụọcha nọrụ na-eme garị bịa-egbusi ikpere na ihu Jisọs sị a, “Onyenwoayị, ya ọ bụrụnwa na o heri gi, i nworu ikike ime na ụhụọchaa ala m.”

En: Jesus reached out his hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” he said. “Be clean!” Immediately he was cleansed of his leprosy.
Ib: Jisọs setie ẹka detu ya nwokem sị a, “O heri m, nworu onwogu!” Na ya nzizi aanịm, ya nwokem bụzuru onye a gwọrụ ụhụọcha.

En: Then Jesus said to him, “See that you don’t tell anyone. But go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
Ib: Jisọs sị ya nwokem a gwọrụ ụhụọcha, “Na ọ dịkwa onye ị na-ịkparị ihe merini. Garịm la ihuanị je-egusi nde ọchụẹja onwogu. Wete ihom iwu Mosisi kwuru na-anịje igusi na-agwọrụ madụ ụhụọcha. Na ọ bụrụ ihe ịgba ama na ihu ọha na-asachawo gụ.”

En: The Faith of the Centurion
Ib: Onye Ọchịaga Nde Rom Nworu Okwukwe

En: When Jesus had entered Capernaum, a centurion came to him, asking for help.
Ib: Mgbe Jisọs gabatarị Kapanọm, onye ọchịaga nde Rom aanị garị jekwute e, bịa na-egoro e sị a,

En: “Lord,” he said, “my servant lies at home paralyzed, suffering terribly.”
Ib: “Onyenwoayị, ẹnwụmaa anwụ-jisiwo nwaọrụ m ụhụ. Ọ tọgbọọrụrị na ulo na-ata ahụhụ.”

En: Jesus said to him, “Shall I come and heal him?”
Ib: Jisọs sị a, “Gaa na mụ eeje je-agwọa ya.”

En: The centurion replied, “Lord, I do not deserve to have you come under my roof. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
Ib: Ọbụ na ya onye ọchịagam sịrị Jisọs, “Onyenwoayị, erugu m eru ka onye i je-ịbịa na ulo e, kama keyenwe na ibie kwufu okwu na ihe na-eme nwaọrụ m alaga.

En: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and that one, ‘Come,’ and he comes. I say to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
Ib: Maka na mụoni nwom nde nọ m na elu na ọchịchị, nwokokwenuru nde aga nọ m na okpuru m na-achị. Onye m sị ‘Bịa na ibie,’ na ọ bịa, m sị onye ọzọ ‘Jee na ibom,’ na o jege. Nwa-ọrụ m m sị ‘Me ẹɦụa,’ na o mie ye.”

En: When Jesus heard this, he was amazed and said to those following him, “Truly I tell you, I have not found anyone in Israel with such great faith.
Ib: Mgbe Jisọs nụdụrụ ihe nwokie kwuru, ya o ju e ẹnya, ya ọ sị ndem soru eni, “Na eziokwu ọ dịgị onye m hụworu na Izirẹlụ nworu otue okwukwie nwokie nwo.

En: I say to you that many will come from the east and the west, and will take their places at the feast with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.
Ib: Ana m akacharị a unu, ntụtụ madụ je-ehi na ọwụwa ẹnyanwụ maa na ọdịda ẹnyanwụ, bịa-anọdụa na oriri woa Eburaham maa Aịziki yaa Jekọb na Alịeze Elugwe.

En: But the subjects of the kingdom will be thrown outside, into the darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”
Ib: Ọbụ na ndem kwesihudiri ịnọ na ya Alịezem je-abụ nde a je-achụfụ na wo eje je[1]anọdụa na ya ime ẹtụlịm, ibe ịkwa ẹkwa yaa ịta ikikere eze je-adị.”

En: Then Jesus said to the centurion, “Go! Let it be done just as you believed it would.” And his servant was healed at that moment.
Ib: Jisọs tụgarịa sị ya nwoke onye ọchịagam, “Laa, na e mieri gi e ẹɦụm i kweyeri na ọ je-ọdị.” Na ya mgbemkọm nwa-ọrụa nke nwokie nwote onwoe, ụhụ dịzu e ma.

En: Jesus Heals Many
Ib: Jisọs Gwọa Ntụtụ Madụ

En: When Jesus came into Peter’s house, he saw Peter’s mother-in-law lying in bed with a fever.
Ib: Mgbe Jisọs gabatarị ulo Pita, ya ọ bụrụ ibe ne nyee ye zune na ugbo, ivoyi jiri e.

En: He touched her hand and the fever left her, and she got up and began to wait on him.
Ib: Jisọs gidie na ẹka, gwọa ya ya ụhụkam. Ya ọ pa[1]vuru na-emegezuru eri ihe.

En: When evening came, many who were demon-possessed were brought to him, and he drove out the spirits with a word and healed all the sick.
Ib: Mgbe o ruru na mgbẹnyasị, nde madụ na-ekuteri Jisọs nde maaọjọọ jigeri, Jisọs jiri okwu ọnụ a na-achụfụsị ya maaọjọọmga, na-agwọkọga nde ụhụ aadịgadịgị ma.

En: This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah: “He took up our infirmities and bore our diseases.”
Ib: Ihie bụrụ iji mezue ihe onye amụ[1]ma Ayịzaya deri na Ẹkwụkwọ Nsọ sị, “O welehiwo ntaram-ahụhụ aayị, vulehi ụhụka aayị oohu.”

En: The Cost of Following Jesus
Ib: Ihe O Je-ori Iso Jisọs

En: When Jesus saw the crowd around him, he gave orders to cross to the other side of the lake.
Ib: MgbeJisọs hụrụ ntụtụ madụ gbarị a gburugburu, ya ọ sị na wo gabuge na ndabu ẹnyụm Galili.

En: Then a teacher of the law came to him and said, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”
Ib: Onye ozizi iwu Mosisi aanị garị jekwute Jisọs bịa-asị a, “Onye ozizi, eje m eso gu je ibe ọọbụla i jije.”

En: Jesus replied, “Foxes have dens and birds have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay his head.”
Ib: Jisọs sị a, “Anụọhịa nwoge mkputu, nnụnụ nwogedueri ẹkwịnị, ọbụ na Nwa Nke Madụ enwogu ibe o na-ohibe isi.”

En: Another disciple said to him, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”
Ib: Onye ọzọ na nde na-eso ụzọ Jisọs sị a, “Onyenwoayị, na mụ ejehee je-akwadụhaa ozu nna m.”

En: But Jesus told him, “Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead.”
Ib: Ọbụ na Jisọs sịrị a, “So m, hasịarị nde nwụhụrụ anwụhụ ozu na wo kwaje.”

En: Jesus Calms the Storm
Ib: Jisọs Kwụsị Oke Akpara Mini

En: Then he got into the boat and his disciples followed him.
Ib: Mgbe Jisọs bayeri na ụgbọ, nde na-eso ụzọ a soko e baye.

En: Suddenly a furious storm came up on the lake, so that the waves swept over the boat. But Jesus was sleeping.
Ib: E jehubeturu, oke uhuhe tụlie akpa[1]ra mini, nke na ụgbọ nọrụ na-achọ okpukpu. Ọbụ na Jisọs nọrụrị na ụra na ime ụgbọ.

En: The disciples went and woke him, saying, “Lord, save us! We’re going to drown!”
Ib: Wo garị jege je-emetie ye sị, “Onyenwoayị, pavuru zọfụta ayị! Mini na-achọ ayị oriri!”

En: He replied, “You of little faith, why are you so afraid?” Then he got up and rebuked the winds and the waves, and it was completely calm.
Ib: Jisọs sị wo, “Ọ bụ gịnị meri unu na-asọ otue ụjọa? Unua ndie okwukwe wo eehigi ne.” Jisọs pavuru vachikote ya ihuhem maa akpara minim ẹnya, ibeaha daa pịam.

En: The men were amazed and asked, “What kind of man is this? Even the winds and the waves obey him!”
Ib: Ya o jukote wo ẹnya ihe gbarịnị, wo sị, “Ọ bụ otue madụ gịnị dị ẹɦụa? Ihuhe maa akpara mini na-erubekogeri e isi.”

En: Jesus Restores Two Demon-Possessed Men
Ib: Ọgwụgwọ Ndikom Ẹbọọ Maa Ọjọọ Jiri

En: When he arrived at the other side in the region of the Gadarenes, two demon-possessed men coming from the tombs met him. They were so violent that no one could pass that way.
Ib: Mgbe wo dabugeri ndabu ya ẹnyụmmụ, na ọnụmara alị nde Gadara, nde dimkpa ẹbọọ maaọ-jọọ jiri hi na ọtụtẹja garị jekwute Jisọs. Wo dịrị ikike dị ọjọọ ọkam nke na ọ dịdịgị onye ụjọ na-ekwe ga ya ọtụtẹjam wo nọrụ ụzọ.

En: “What do you want with us, Son of God?” they shouted. “Have you come here to torture us before the appointed time?”
Ib: Wo tie mkpu sị Jisọs, “Ndaa ihe ayịa gị jiko, Ọkpara Chineke? Ị bịawo ịta ayị ahụhụ mgbe ogie aaka erugu?”

En: Some distance from them a large herd of pigs was feeding.
Ib: O nworu igwe ezi nọrụ na ndaga ya ibom na-akpa nri.

En: The demons begged Jesus, “If you drive us out, send us into the herd of pigs.”
Ib: Ya maaọjọọmga gororu Jisọs sị a, “Ya ọ bụrụ na ị je-achụfụta ayị na ime ndie ayị ji, chụba ayị na igwe ezimga.”

En: He said to them, “Go!” So they came out and went into the pigs, and the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and died in the water.
Ib: Jisọs sị wo, “Unu jee!” Wo hi na ime ya ndem wo jiri fụta je-agabadụa na ya igwe ezimga. Ya ezim na ohu chịsị ọsọ je-awụbaa na ime ẹnyụm, nwụhụdụa.

En: Those tending the pigs ran off, went into the town and reported all this, including what had happened to the demon-possessed men.
Ib: Nde nọrụ na-achị ya ezimga kpefu ọsọ mgbe wo hụrụ ihe gbarịnị, garị je-akpaarị nde nọ na ezi ihe meri ya ezi womga maa ihe gbaarị ndem maaọjọọ jiri.

En: Then the whole town went out to meet Jesus. And when they saw him, they pleaded with him to leave their region.
Ib: Ya nde alịm kwagbụkọ na-ejekwu Jisọs. Mgbe wo hụrụ a, wo gororu e sị a bikoo sọhụrụ wo na alị wo.

En: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle and set apart for the gospel of God—
Ib: Ọ bụ m Pọl, nwaọrụ Karaịs Jisọs, onye Chineke kuru ịbụ onyeozi Karaịs a họtarị izise oziọma bayeri Chineke na-ederi unu ẹkwụkwọa.

En: the gospel he promised beforehand through his prophets in the Holy Scripture
Ib: Oziọma Chineke jiri nde amụma a kwe nkwa ẹkamgbe dịka nke e deri e na Ẹkwụkwọ Nsọ,

En: regarding his Son, who as to his earthly life was a descendant of David,
Ib: ihe bayeri Ọkpara a, onye bịarị na ụwa dịka madụ hite na eriri Devidi.

En: and who through the Spirit of holiness was appointed the Son of God in power by his resurrection from the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord.
Ib: Chineke gusiri na ọ bụ Ọkpara a hite na omumie na o hi na ọnwụ pavuru na ike nke Maa Nsọ: Jisọs Karaịs Onyenwoayị.

En: Through him we received grace and apostleship to call all the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith for his name’s sake.
Ib: Chineke kwobe Jisọs Karaịs gusi ayị ẹwụọma a, me ayị bụrụ ndeozi Karaịs je-ekufute ntụtụ madụ na etiti nde aabụgụ nde Juu, na wo sokoru ruberi Chineke isi, nwoe ntụkwasịobu maka ẹha a.

En: And you also are among those Gentiles who are called to belong to Jesus Christ.
Ib: Unuande Rom sokozu na ya ndem Chineke kuru na unu bụkọzuru ndeke Jisọs Karaịs.

En: To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be his holy people: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
Ib: Ana m ederi unu oohu nde bu na Rom ẹkwụkwọa, bụ nde Chineke hụrụ na ẹnya, ku wo, ịbụ ndekie dị nsọ. Na udo yaa ẹwụọma Chineke bụ Nnade aayị yaa nke Jisọs Karaịs bụ Onyenwoayị dịrị unu.

En: Paul’s Longing to Visit Rome
Ib: Ya Ọ Gụa Pọl Ẹgụ Ije Rom

En: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being reported all over the world.
Ib: Nke mbụ, aga m ẹka Jisọs Karaịs na-ekele Chineke m na isi uunu, maka a na-akpa ihe baye[1]ri okwukwe uunu na ụwa na ohu.

En: God, whom I serve in my spirit in preaching the gospel of his Son, is my witness how constantly I remember you
Ib: Chineke, Onye m ji obu m na ohu na-ejeri ezise oziọma bayeri Ọkpara a, bụ onye ẹkebe m na ana m arịta unu

En: in my prayers at all times; and I pray that now at last by God’s will the way may be opened for me to come to you.
Ib: mgbe ọọbụla na ekpere. Ana m egororu Chineke ya ọ bụrụ na ọ chọrụ a, na o meheeri m ụzọ na mụ eenwo ike ịkpakwute unu.

En: I long to see you so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to make you strong—
Ib: Ọ na-ọgụ m ẹgụ ọkam ịhụ unu, ma m nwo ike weteri unu ụfọdị ihe ọnịnị nke ime maa, ma unu guzosie ike.

En: that is, that you and I may be mutually encouraged by each other’s faith.
Ib: Ọ bụ ahịaga ma ayị gbatarị onwaayị ume na okwukwe ayị nwo.

En: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers and sisters, that I planned many times to come to you (but have been prevented from doing so until now) in order that I might have a harvest among you, just as I have had among the other Gentiles.
Ib: Achọgụ m na unu amakwa, ụmụnna, na ọ dịwo akpa ntụtụ ẹkamgbe m hịhịadụrụ ma m bịa nke uunu. Ọbụ na o nwom ihe na-egbochu mụ eni tututu rute ẹɦụọdị. Obu m bụ ma m nwo ike kuteri Jisọs nde na-eso ụzọ a na etiti uunu ẹɦụm m nwoteduworu na mba ọzọga nde aabụgụ nde Juu.

En: I am obligated both to Greeks and non-Greeks, both to the wise and the foolish.
Ib: Eji m mba oohu ụgwọ, maa nde bụ nde Giriki maa nde aabụgụ, maa nde maarị ihe maa nde aadịgị nke wo maarị.

En: That is why I am so eager to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome.
Ib: Ọ bụ a meri Ẹkwụkwọ Pọl Dejeeri Nde Rom ọ na-ọgụsi m ẹgụ ike iziko unuande nọ na Rom oziọma. Ikike Oziọma

En: For I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God that brings salvation to everyone who believes: first to the Jew, then to the Gentile.
Ib: Izi oziọma adịgị m egwu, maka na ọ bụ a bụ ikike Chineke ji na-azọfụta ụmụ madụ, nde kwerini: hitehee na nde Juu ta na o rubeje nde aabụgụ nde Juu.

En: For in the gospel the righteousness of God is revealed—a righteousness that is by faith from first to last, just as it is written: “The righteous will live by faith.”
Ib: Maka na ọ bụ na ime ya oziọmaa bụ ibe e kpuheri ụmara-ọma nke Chineke. Ọ dabeeri hite na isi rue na ọgwụgwụ na onwunwo okwukwe. Dịka nke e deri e na Ẹkwụkwọ Nsọ, “Nde ụmara-ọma je-adị ndụ hite na okwukwe wo.”

En: God’s Wrath Against Sinful Humanity
Ib: Iwe-ọkụ Chineke Na Ibe Ụmụ Madụ Nọ

En: The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of people, who suppress the truth by their wickedness,
Ib: E hiwo na elugwe gusi iwe[1]ọkụ Chineke na ibe ụmụ madụ nọ, maka ihe ọjọọ wo yaa arụrụalị wo na-arụ, eekwegi na ya eziokwum bayeri Chineke fụta ihe.

En: since what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them.
Ib: Iwe-ọkụ Chineke na-adakwasị wo maka na o gusituwo wo ihe ọọbụla wo kwesiri ịma bayeri Chineke.

En: For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities—his eternal power and divine nature—have been clearly seen, being understood from what has been made, so that people are without excuse.
Ib: Hiteri na ẹkamgbe okike ụwa, ikikie aagwụgụ agwụ yaa ihom na ohu o jiri bụrụ Chineke, madụ eenwogu ike ịhụ ẹnya, Chineke emewo ahụtatuem nke wo dị. E nwo ike ịgọta wo hite na ihe oohu o keri eke, nke na madụ adịgị ihe o ji je-agọ ẹgụgọ na ihu Chineke.

En: For although they knew God, they neither glorified him as God nor gave thanks to him, but their thinking became futile and their foolish hearts were darkened.
Ib: Na mgbe wo madụụrụm na ọ bụ a bụ Chineke, ka wo aasọfụrụ a ka Chineke, nịgị a otuto yaa ekele ruturu eni, kama ọrịrị wo bụrụ ihe amaka, obu iberibe wo techuhudue.

En: Although they claimed to be wise, they became fools
Ib: Wo na-asị na wo bụ nde maarị ihe, ọbụ na wo bụ nde iberibe.

En: and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images made to look like a mortal human being and birds and animals and reptiles.
Ib: Kama wo je na-ekperi Chineke onye ebube aanwụhụgụ anwụhụ, wo je-apịtadụa ihe wo pịrị na oyiye madụ amaka na-anwụhụ anwụhụ, ma ọ bụgụ na ụdịdị nnụnụ, ma ọ bụgụ na ụdịdị anụ kwụ ọkpa, ma ọ bụgụ na ụdịdị ihe na-arịga arị, debe na-ekperi.

En: Therefore God gave them over in the sinful desires of their hearts to sexual impurity for the degrading of their bodies with one another.
Ib: Ọ bụ a meri Chineke wefuuru wo ẹka wo je-emeje nke dị wo ma. Wo wụjube na-eme ihe rụrụ arụ wo kpụtarị na obu wo. Wo na-enwo mmeko nwoke yaa nwanyị aalụtaarịgị onwowo.

En: They exchanged the truth about God for a lie, and worshiped and served created things rather than the Creator—who is forever praised. Amen.
Ib: Wo tụgarịa eziokwu ihe oohu bayeri Chineke weri ụga bube ụzọ, je na-akpọrụ ihe e keri eke isi na alị, na-ejeri e ozi ta hasịa Onyem keri ihe ọọbụla. Onye yaanịa nwo otuto na ohu rue mgbe agwụ-agwụ. Amịn.

En: Because of this, God gave them over to shameful lusts. Even their women exchanged natural sexual relations for unnatural ones.
Ib: Maka na wo meri ya ẹɦụm, Chineke habue wo wo dasiri na-eme ihe mmechu-ihu na-agụ wo ẹgụ na omume. Maa nde ụmụ nwanyị wo agbanwokoduwo mmekorite na nke o kwesiri ịdị, na-emezu nke aabụgụ anị.

En: In the same way the men also abandoned natural relations with women and were inflamed with lust for one another. Men committed shameful acts with other men, and received in themselves the due penalty for their error.
Ib: Nde nwokeko habuzue inwo mmeko nwoke yaa nwanyị nke Chineke deberi e, na-achọzu nwoke ibe wo. Na nwoke yaa nwoke ibie ana-enwo mmeko ana-asọ egwu. Ọ bụ a meri wo na-anata ntaram-ahụhụ kwesiri woni maka omume ihe rụrụ arụ dịga ya ẹɦụm.

En: Furthermore, just as they did not think it worthwhile to retain the knowledge of God, so God gave them over to a depraved mind, so that they do what ought not to be done.
Ib: Ọzọ bụ na maka na wo jụkarị ịmata ihe wo kwesiri ịma bayeri Chineke, Chineke habue wo wo na-akpụta ihe rụrụ arụ na obu wo gbagọrụ agbagọ na-eme. Na-eme ihe eekwesigi ekwesi na wo meri.

En: They have become filled with every kind of wickedness, evil, greed and depravity. They are full of envy, murder, strife, deceit and malice. They are gossips,
Ib: Ụrụ alị dị iche iche ejuwo wo obu; ihe ọjọọ, ẹnya-ukwu yaa ndụ ọjọọ. Wo bụrụ nde ẹnyụhụ, nde na-egbu madụ, nde na-akpa oke, nde ụgọrọ, na-evuru madụ ibe wo ihe na obu, nde na-akpa asịrị,

En: slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant and boastful; they invent ways of doing evil; they disobey their parents;
Ib: nde na-ekwuto madụ ibe wo, nde ihe Chineke aadịgị ma, nde na-akparị madụ, nde mpako yaa ọtamba, nde na-arịfụta nke a ga na-arụ alị na-efu eze elu, nde na-enufuru nde mụrụ wo isi,

En: they have no understanding, no fidelity, no love, no mercy.
Ib: nde amamihe kọrụ, eekwesigi na a tụkwasị wo obu, nde obu-ọjọọ, nde dị ụrụ aahatagị a ahata.

En: Although they know God’s righteous decree that those who do such things deserve death, they not only continue to do these very things but also approve of those who practice them.
Ib: Wo amakọduworu ntụziẹka ọma nke Chineke, na ọnwụ na-eche nde na-eme ihe dị ya ẹɦụm, wo gaam na ihu na-eme ihe wo na-eme. Ka ọ bụnwa na wo na-emie kama wo na-akwagideko nde na-eme ihe dịga ya ẹɦụm.

En: God’s Righteous Judgment
Ib: Ikpe Nkwụm-ọtọ Chineke

En: You, therefore, have no excuse, you who pass judgment on someone else, for at whatever point you judge another, you are condemning yourself, because you who pass judgment do the same things.
Ib: Unuande enwogu ngọfụ ọọbụla mgbe unu na-ekpe nde ọzọ ikpe na ihe ọjọọ wo na-eme. Maka na mgbem i kperi onye ọzọ ikpe, ikpe makọrụ gụ ibe ọ bụ na gịoni na-emeko ihom i kwoberi na-ekpe nde ọzọ ikpe.

En: Now we know that God’s judgment against those who do such things is based on truth.
Ib: Ayị maarị na Chineke ji eziokwu na-ekpe nde na-eme ihe dịga ya ẹɦụm ikpe.

En: So when you, a mere human being, pass judgment on them and yet do the same things, do you think you will escape God’s judgment?
Ib: Unu na-arịị na unuande bụ madụ amaka na-emekoge ihe dị ya ẹɦụm, ta na-ekpe nde na-emieni ikpe je-agbanahị ikpe Chineke?

En: Or do you show contempt for the riches of his kindness, forbearance and patience, not realizing that God’s kindness is intended to lead you to repentance?
Ib: Saa unu na-eleli obuọma maa ndidi yaa nnagide Chineke na-enwo na ibe unu nọ; ọ bụ ahịaga na unu amagị na obuọma Chineke bụnwa ma unu nwo ike tụgarịa habue omume ihe ọjọọ?

En: But because of your stubbornness and your unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath against yourself for the day of God’s wrath, when his righteous judgment will be revealed.
Ib: Ọbụ maka na unu akpọwo ekwe nkụ, mechisie obu uunu ike meri iwe-ọkụ Chineke dị na-echeri unu na ya izuku iwe-ọkụm nke Chineke, mgbe e je-ekpuhe ikpe nkwụm-ọtọ a.

En: God “will repay each person according to what they have done.”
Ib: Na Chineke akwụa madụ oohu ụgwọ-ọrụ ihe oohu wo meri na ụwa.

En: To those who by persistence in doing good seek glory, honor and immortality, he will give eternal life.
Ib: Ndem nọgideri na omume ihe ọma maka na wo nọrụ na-atụ ẹnya ebube yaa mpali elu maa anwụhụgụ anwụhụ, Chineke je-anị wo ndụ agwụ-agwụ.

En: But for those who are self-seeking and who reject the truth and follow evil, there will be wrath and anger.
Ib: Ọbụ na ndem ihe bayeri onwowo dachiri obu, jụkarị ya eziokwum nke Chineke, na-ebu isi kpụlịkpụlị na omume ihe ọjọọ; Chineke je-eweri wo iwe, weri iwe-ọkụ a mesie wo ike.

En: There will be trouble and distress for every human being who does evil: first for the Jew, then for the Gentile;
Ib: Ndem na ohu na-etiye ẹka na omume ihe ọjọọ je-ahụsi ẹnya, jie ihe ọkụ, hite na nde Juu bụ nde o je-obu ụzọ rube ta na ọ gazue ndem aabụgụ nde Juu.

En: but glory, honor and peace for everyone who does good: first for the Jew, then for the Gentile.
Ib: Ọbụ na Chineke je-eji ebube, mpali elu yaa udo gọzie ndem na-eme ihe ọma: hitekweri na nde Juu bụ nde je-ebute ụzọ, ta na o zue nde aabụgụ nde Juu.

En: For God does not show favoritism.
Ib: Maka na Chineke elegi madụ ẹnya na ihu ma ya o kpefue ikpe.

En: All who sin apart from the law will also perish apart from the law, and all who sin under the law will be judged by the law.
Ib: Nde aabụgụ nde Juu aamagị ihe bayeri iwum Chineke nịrị Mosisi, wo mie ihe ọjọọ na Chineke ekpie wo ikpe na-ejigi ya iwum. Taa nde Juu bụ nde a nịrị ya iwum, wo mie ihe ọjọọ na Chineke ejiri ya iwum kpie wo ikpe.

En: For it is not those who hear the law who are righteous in God’s sight, but it is those who obey the law who will be declared righteous.
Ib: Maka na ọ bụgụ nde nụrụ ihe ya iwum kwuru bụ nde a na-agụye na nde ụmara-ọma na ihu Chineke, kama ọ bụ nde ruberi isi mie ihe e deri na iwu bụ nde a gụrụ na nde ụmara-ọma.

En: (Indeed, when Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by nature things required by the law, they are a law for themselves, even though they do not have the law.
Ib: Maka na ya ọ bụrụ na nde aabụgụ nde Juu, bụ nde aanịdịgị ya iwum, akpụtam na obu wo mie ihe ya iwum chọrụ, ị hụgụ na wo abụworu nde deberi iwu, na-agbayegi na a nịdịgị wo iwu.

En: They show that the requirements of the law are written on their hearts, their consciences also bearing witness, and their thoughts sometimes accusing them and at other times even defending them.)
Ib: Na ụmara wo egusiwo na-agbarị ihe ya iwum kwuru na ime obu wo. Ọ bụkọ nke obu wo je na-ama wo ikpe ma ọ bụgụ na-akarị wo na ihe wo meri dị ma.

En: This will take place on the day when God judges people’s secrets through Jesus Christ, as my gospel declares.
Ib: Ihie na ohu je-afụta ihe na ya izukum, mgbe Chineke je-aga ẹka Jisọs Karaịs kpie madụ oohu ikpe. Wefutedue ihe oohu zoru ezo na ime obu ụmụ madụ dịka nke m ziri na oziọma m.

En: The Jews and the Law
Ib: Ihe Bayeri Iwu Yaa Nde Juu

En: Now you, if you call yourself a Jew; if you rely on the law and boast in God;
Ib: A bịa na unuande na-eku onwuunu nde Juu; unu na-adaberi na iwu, na-aba mba na unu bụ ndeke Chineke;

En: if you know his will and approve of what is superior because you are instructed by the law;
Ib: unu amaduworu ihe bụ ọchụchọ Chineke, marị ihe dị ma yaa nke aadịgị ma na ihu e, maka na e ziri e unu na iwu.

En: if you are convinced that you are a guide for the blind, a light for those who are in the dark,
Ib: Unu maarị, ya o due unu ẹnya na unu bụ nde na-edu ndem kpuru isi, bụrụ ihe dịrị ndem nọ na ẹtụlị,

En: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of little children, because you have in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth—
Ib: unu bụrụ nde na-akpaziche nde iberibe ihu, na-ezi ụmụrụma ihe, maka na unu nwo ya iwum bụ ezumoke nke amamihe yaa eziokwu.

En: you, then, who teach others, do you not teach yourself? You who preach against stealing, do you steal?
Ib: Unuande na-ezi nde ọzọ ihe, unu ezikogu onwuunu? Unuande na-ezi nde ọzọ wo ezusi ohi, unu na-avụnarị nde madụ ihe wo?

En: You who say that people should not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?
Ib: Unuande na-ezi nde ọzọ wo ejesi na nyee madụ, unu na-eje na nyee nde ọzọ? Unuande eekwegi ihe ẹrụsị, unu ejegi wo ezunete ihe ẹrụsị?

En: You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God by breaking the law?
Ib: Unuande na-aba na-anịrị unu iwu, unu na-eweteri Chineke mkparị hite na emebi ya iwum?

En: As it is written: “God’s name is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.”
Ib: Dịka nke e deri e na Ẹkwụkwọ Nsọ: “Maka unuande Juu, a na-ekwuto ẹha Chineke na etiti nde aabụgụ nde Juu.”

En: Circumcision has value if you observe the law, but if you break the law, you have become as though you had not been circumcised.
Ib: Gị mie ihe iwu na-achọ, osise ọnutu abagị uru ọọbụla; ọbụ na gị bụrụ onye na-emebi iwu, na ị marị na gịa onye eesedigi ọnutu ham.

En: So then, if those who are not circumcised keep the law’s requirements, will they not be regarded as though they were circumcised?
Ib: Ya ọ bụrụ na ndem eesedigi ọnutu emie ihom e deri na iwu, ọ bụ na a magị agụye wo na nde e seri ọnụ-utu?

En: The one who is not circumcised physically and yet obeys the law will condemn you who, even though you have the written code and circumcision, are a lawbreaker.
Ib: Ọ bụ nde aabụgụ nde Juu je-ama unuande Juu ikpe; na-agbayegi na-eseri unu ọnụ-utu, gbaa ya iwum agba nịa unu, unu na-emebi iwu. Ọbụ na wo na-edebe iwu na-agbayegi na-esedigi wo ọnutu nke anụhụ.

En: A person is not a Jew who is one only outwardly, nor is circumcision merely outward and physical.
Ib: Madụ abụgụ onye Juu ma ya ọ bụrụ anwa na elu ụhụ, ka osise ọnutu aadị ihe ọ fụtarị ma ya ọ bụ[1]rụnwa nke elu ụhụ.

En: No, a person is a Jew who is one inwardly; and circumcision is circumcision of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code. Such a person’s praise is not from other people, but from God.
Ib: Kamahudi onye Juu bụ onyem bụ anị na ime obu; osise ọnutu bụrụ ọmụanịm e seri na ime obu, nke Maa Nsọ meri. Ọ bụgụ nke hiteri na edebe iwum e deri ede, kama ọ bụ Maa Nsọ na-arụ a. Nde dị ya ẹɦụm bụ Chineke na-etoye wo, wo anatagị otuto na ẹka madụ. Chineke Onye Kwesiri Ntụkwasịobu

En: God’s Faithfulness
Ib: Chineke Onye Kwesiri Ntụkwasịobu

En: What advantage, then, is there in being a Jew, or what value is there in circumcision?
Ib: Ndaa uru ọ barị na madụ bụ onye Juu karịa nde aabụgụ nde Juu, ma ọ bụgụ ndaa uru onye e seri ọnutu riteri karịa onyem eesedigi ọnụ-utu?

En: Much in every way! First of all, the Jews have been entrusted with the very words of God.
Ib: Ọ barị uru ọkam na ụzọ dị iche iche! Nke mbụ, ọ bụ wo bụ nde Chineke weeri okwu e ye na ẹka.

En: What if some were unfaithful? Will their unfaithfulness nullify God’s faithfulness?
Ib: Ya ọ bụrụ na o nwo nde ụfọdị eekwesigi na-atụkwasị wo obu, o je-ome ka Chineke eekwesisi na 3 a tụkwasị a obu?

En: Not at all! Let God be true, and every human being a liar. As it is written: “So that you may be proved right when you speak and prevail when you judge.”
Ib: Ọ gbakwagị agba! Chineke yaanịa bụrụ onye eziokwu, na ụmụ madụ oohu bụrụ nde ụga. Dịka nke e deri e na Ẹkwụkwọ Nsọ: “Na mgbe ikwuru okwu na ọ bụrụ eziokwu, e kpie gie ka ikpe na o bueri gi.”

En: But if our unrighteousness brings out God’s righteousness more clearly, what shall we say? That God is unjust in bringing his wrath on us? (I am using a human argument.)
Ib: Ya ọ bụrụ na-emechegi emeche aayị wefutecheri gusi na Chineke na-emeche emeche, ndaa ihe ayị nworu ike ikwu? Ọ fụtarị ahịaga na Chineke meluru ma ya o weso ayịande meluruni iwe-ọkụ? Ekwuru m okwu e ka madụ amaka.

En: Certainly not! If that were so, how could God judge the world?
Ib: Ọ dịgị nke Chineke garị meluu! Ya ọ bụrụ na Chineke abụgụ onye ikpe nkwụm-ọtọ, ọ ga ẹgaa je je-ekpe ụwa oohu ikpe?

En: Someone might argue, “If my falsehood enhances God’s truthfulness and so increases his glory, why am I still condemned as a sinner?”
Ib: Ụfọdị nworu ike na-asị, “Ya ọ bụrụ na ịga ụga m na-ewefuteche nke Chineke garị bụrụ onye eziokwu yaa ebubie, a gakwakwarị ẹgaa na-ama m ikpe na-abụ m onye ihe ọjọọ?”

En: Why not say—as some slanderously claim that we say—“Let us do evil that good may result”? Their condemnation is just!
Ib: Ọ bụnụ a bụ na a je na-asịgazuu dịka nde ụfọdị na-agabo ayị ụga na ayị na-ekwukogezuu, “Na ayị meje ihe ọjọọ ma nke ọma gbaje.” Ikpe je-amatu wom nke o kwesiri.

En: No One Is Righteous
Ib: Ọ Dịgị Onye Bụ Onye Ụmara-ọma

En: What shall we conclude then? Do we have any advantage? Not at all! For we have already made the charge that Jews and Gentiles alike are all under the power of sin.
Ib: Ndaa ihe je-abụ oburu ikpe aayị? Ayị ka nde ọzọ ma? Ma a ga a ẹgaa? Ayị hiworuri gbue ikoro waa ya eze! Na nde Juu maa nde aabụgụ nde Juu bụtum nde ihe ọjọọ.

En: As it is written: “There is no one righteous, not even one;
Ib: Dịka nke e deri e na Ẹkwụkwọ Nsọ: “Ọ dịgị onye bụ onye ụmara-ọma, ọ dịgị ma ọ bụgụ onye aanị;

En: there is no one who understands; there is no one who seeks God.
Ib: ọ dịgị onye nworu ngọta, ọ dịgị onye na-achọ Chineke.

En: All have turned away, they have together become worthless; there is no one who does good, not even one.”
Ib: Wo oohu agbayeworu Chineke azụ; wo oohu abụworum ihe oheri; ọ dịgị onye na-eme ihe dị ma, ọ dịgị ma ọ bụgụ onye aanị.”

En: “Their throats are open graves; their tongues practice deceit.”“The poison of vipers is on their lips.”
Ib: “Wo jaa ọnụ na ọ dịa ka e kpuheri ili, na okwu oohu hi wo na ire abụrụ ụga ụga.” “Na okwu hi wo na ogborọnụ ana-egbu ka ibe agwọ tarị madụ.”

En: “Their mouths are full of cursing and bitterness.”
Ib: “Ihe juru wom ọnụ bụ odudu ikwu yaa okwu ọjọọ.”

En: “Their feet are swift to shed blood;
Ib: “Ọkpa na-adịwo nkọ ije ogbugbu madụ;

En: ruin and misery mark their ways,
Ib: ibe ọọbụla wo gabugeri bụm emebi ihe yaa ọlịla ihe na iyi bụ ihe a na-ahụ.

En: and the way of peace they do not know.”
Ib: Wo amagị nke aga na-ebu na udo.”

En: “There is no fear of God before their eyes.”
Ib: “Wo asọtụgụm Chineke asọ na ndụ wo.”

En: Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God.
Ib: Ọbụ na ayị maarị na ihe ọọbụ[1]la iwu kwuru dịịrị ndem bu na okpuru iwu. Na madụ oohu tụba ire na ọnụ, maka na onye ọọbụla na ụwa je-eguzo na ihu Chineke sarị ọnụ a.

En: Therefore no one will be declared righteous in God’s sight by the works of the law; rather, through the law we become conscious of our sin.
Ib: Ọ dịgị onye ọọbụla a je-asị na ọ bụ onye ụmara-ọma na ihu Chineke maka na o deberi iwu, kama, iwu bịarị bịa-eme ayị marị na ayị bụ nde ihe ọjọọ.

En: Righteousness Through Faith
Ib: Ịbụ Onye Ụmara-ọma Hite Na Ntụkwasịobu

En: But now apart from the law the righteousness of God has been made known, to which the Law and the Prophets testify.
Ib: Ẹɦụọdị, e egusiwo ụmara-ọma hi na Chineke aabụgụ hite na edebe iwu. Ọ bụ a bụ ụzọm Iwu yaa nde amụma gbarị ama a.

En: This righteousness is given through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe. There is no difference between Jew and Gentile,
Ib: Ụmaraọmaa hi na Chineke na-ehite na madụ inwo ntụkwasịobu na Jisọs Karaịs. Chineke na-anabata onye ọọbụla nworu okwukwe na Jisọs Karaịs na-akpagị oke.

En: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
Ib: Maka na madụ oohu emewo ihe ọjọọ erusigi inwote ebube Chineke.

En: and all are justified freely by his grace through the redemption that came by Christ Jesus.
Ib: Chineke ji ẹwụọma a na-agbafụta madụ oohu na ihe ọjọọ na amaka. Ọ garị ẹka Karaịs Jisọs mieri ayị a.

En: God presented Christ as a sacrifice of atonement, through the shedding of his blood—to be received by faith. He did this to demonstrate his righteousness, because in his forbearance he had left the sins committed beforehand unpunished—
Ib: Chineke jiri Jisọs chụa ẹja udo maka ihe ọjọọ aayị na ọnwụ a. Ya o weri mee ye me iwe-ọkụ Chineke dajụa na isi ndem nworu ntụkwasịobu na Jisọs Karaịs. Chineke meri e ya ẹɦụm igusi na ọ bụ onye ikpe ọma, maka na o nworu ogologo ntachiobu ka ọọta ndem megeri ihe ọjọọ ẹkamgbe ichie ahụhụ.

En: he did it to demonstrate his righteousness at the present time, so as to be just and the one who justifies those who have faith in Jesus.
Ib: Chineke meri ya ẹɦụm igusi na ọ bụ Onye ụmara-ọma na echeri e ayị nọ na ya. I gusikokwenu na ọ bụ onye ikpe ọma na-azọfụta nde nworu ntụkwasịobu na Jisọs.

En: Where, then, is boasting? It is excluded. Because of what law? The law that requires works? No, because of the law that requires faith.
Ib: Ndakwanụa ihe madụ ji je-aba mba? Ọ dịsịgị! A garị ẹgaa mieri ayị a? Ọ bụ maka edebe iwu? Waa, kama ọ bụ maka inwo okwukwe.

En: For we maintain that a person is justified by faith apart from the works of the law.
Ib: Maka na ayị na-ekwubu okwu na a na-anabata madụ na ihu Chineke hite na okwukwe onye ọ bụ nwo, ọ bụgụ na onye ọ bụ bụ onye na-edebe iwu.

En: Or is God the God of Jews only? Is he not the God of Gentiles too? Yes, of Gentiles too,
Ib: Chineke ọ bụ nke nde Juu wo aanị wo? Ọ bụkọgụ Chineke nde aabụgụ nde Juu? Ọ bụkọ Chineke nde aabụgụ nde Juu.

En: since there is only one God, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through that same faith.
Ib: Maka na e nwonwe Chineke aanị, onye na-eme nde e seri ọnutu na wo abụrụ nde a nabatarị na ihu e hite na okwukwe wo, maa nde eesegi ọnutu na wo abụkọrụ nde a nabatarị na ihu e hiteko na okwukwe wo nwo.

En: Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith? Not at all! Rather, we uphold the law.
Ib: Ọ fụtarị ahịaga na onwunwo okwukwe kagbuzuru Iwu? Waakwa, ọ bụgụ ya ẹɦụm, kamahudi ayị na-akwagide Iwu.

En: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, discovered in this matter?
Ib: Ndaa ihe ayị je-asị na Eburaham, nnade ochoroche aayị chọfụtarị na okwu e?

En: If, in fact, Abraham was justified by works, he had something to boast about—but not before God.
Ib: Ya ọ bụrụ na eziokwu na a gụrụ Eburaham na onye a nabatarị na ihu Chineke maka ihe ọ rụrụ, na unu amarị na o nworu ihe o kwesiri iji baa mba, ọbụ na ọ bụgụ na ihu Chineke.

En: What does Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”
Ib: Ẹkwụkwọ nsọ kwudiri gịnị? “Eburaham kweteeri Chineke, a gụyeri e ye ka onye ụmara-ọma.”

En: Now to the one who works, wages are not credited as a gift but as an obligation.
Ib: Ọ na-ọbụje madụ rụa ọrụ na a kwụa ya ụgwọ-ọrụ a. Anagị asịje na a nịrị a ihe kama ọ bụ ihe o jiri ẹka a kpata.

En: However, to the one who does not work but trusts God who justifies the ungodly, their faith is credited as righteousness.
Ib: Ọbụ na a na-agụ nde madụ nde ụmara-ọma na abụgụ maka ọrụ wo rụrụ, kama ọ bụ maka okwukwe wo nwo na Chineke na-agbaharị nde ihe ọjọọ.

En: David says the same thing when he speaks of the blessedness of the one to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:
Ib: Devidi kwukoru okwu bayeri ihe dị ya ẹɦụm na mgbe o kwuru okwu sị na onyem aadịgị ihe ọ rụrụ kama ya o nwoe ntụkwasịobu, Chineke gụa Onye Ụmara-ọma bụ onye a gọziri agọzi: 274 Nde Rom

En: “Blessed are those whose transgressions are forgiven, whose sins are covered.
Ib: “Ndem a gbahawooru ihe ọjọọ wo, bụ ndem e welehiworu ihe ọjọọ wo, bụ nde a gọziri agọzi.

En: Blessed is the one whose sin the Lord will never count against them.”
Ib: Onyem Onyenwoayị aamagị arịtasị ihe ọjọọ ya, bụ onye a gọziri agọzi.”

En: Is this blessedness only for the circumcised, or also for the uncircumcised? We have been saying that Abraham’s faith was credited to him as righteousness.
Ib: Ya ngọzie Devidi kwuru okwu e, ọ bụ nke nde e seri ọnutu woanị wo saa o rubekoeri ndem eesedigi ọnụ-utu? Ayị na-ekwu em ẹkamgbe na okwukwe Eburaham nworu meri e jiri gụ a na onye ụmara-ọma.

En: Under what circumstances was it credited? Was it after he was circumcised, or before? It was not after, but before!
Ib: Ndaa ọnọdụ e jiri gụye Eburaham na onye ụmara-ọma? Ọ bụ na mgbe e seworu Eburaham ọnutu saa ọ bụ na mgbe aaka esegi e ọnụ-utu? Nke bụ eziokwu bụ na ọ bụrụ na mgbe aaka esedigi e ọnụ-utu!

En: And he received circumcision as a sign, a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised. So then, he is the father of all who believe but have not been circumcised, in order that righteousness might be credited to them.
Ib: E seri Eburaham ọnutu nke bụ ihe ahụma onye ụmara-ọma, bụ ọnọdụ o jiri okwukwe o nworu nata na mgbe aaka esekoheegi e ọnụ-utu. Ọ bụ a meri Eburaham jiri bụrụ nnade madụ oohu nworu okwukwe na-agbayegi na a ka esegi wo ọnụ-utu, ma a gụ wo na nde ụmara-ọma maka okwukwe wo.

En: And he is then also the father of the circumcised who not only are circumcised but who also follow in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised.
Ib: Eburaham bụ nna ndem e seri ọnụ-utu, bụ nde aabụgụnwa na e seri wo ọnutu kama na-ebuko ndụm nnade aayị Eburaham buru, bụ inwo okwukwe na mgbe aaka esekoheegi e ọnụ-utu.

En: It was not through the law that Abraham and his offspring received the promise that he would be heir of the world, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.
Ib: Eburaham yaa nde nwanwa a wo anatadịgị nkwam Chineke kweri wo na wo je-eri ekpie na ụwa maka na wo nọrụ na-edebe iwu, kama ọ bụrụ maka ya okwukwem wo nworu merini e jiri gụ wo na Nde Ụmara-ọma.

En: For if those who depend on the law are heirs, faith means nothing and the promise is worthless,
Ib: Maka na ya ọ bụrụ na ọ bụ nde na-edebe iwu je-eri ya ekpem bụ ahịaga na ọ dịgị uru inwo okwukwe barị, dịkwanụgụ ihe ya nkwam Chineke kweri fụtarị.

En: because the law brings wrath. And where there is no law there is no transgression.
Ib: Maka na ọ bụ iwu na-ewete iwe-ọkụ Chineke. Ibe iwu aadịgị ka ọdịda na iwu aadịkọ.

En: Therefore, the promise comes by faith, so that it may be by grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham’s offspring—not only to those who are of the law but also to those who have the faith of Abraham. He is the father of us all.
Ib: Ọ bụ a meri ya nkwam dabeeri na onwunwo okwukwe, ma ọ bụrụ na hite na ẹwụọma Chineke na o rube ụmụ nwanwa Eburaham na ohu. Ọ bụgụnwa ndem na-edebe iwu, kama maa ndem nworu okwukwe ka Eburaham. Ọ bụ Eburaham bụ nnade aayị oohu.

En: As it is written: “I have made you a father of many nations.” He is our father in the sight of God, in whom he believed—the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being things that were not.
Ib: Dịka nke e deri e na Ẹkwụkwọ Nsọ, “Emewo m gu nna ntụtụ mba dị iche iche.” Ọ bụ Eburaham bụ nnade aayị na ihu Chineke, onyem ọ tụkwasịrị obu. Chineke bụ a na-eme ihe nwụhụrụ anwụhụ na ọ dị ndụ ọzọ, onye ji okwu ọnụ a kie ihe eehigedigi dị wo dị.

En: Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations, just as it had been said to him, “So shall your offspring be.”
Ib: Na mgbe ọọdịsịdịgị ihe o je-ejigide ẹka nwoe olile-ẹnya, Eburaham nọgideri na olile-ẹnya nwoe ntụkwasịobu merini o jiri bụrụ nnade ntụtụ mba dịka Ẹkwụkwọ Nsọ hiri kwue sị, “Nde nwanwa gị wo je-adị ntụtụ ka chichinda dị na elugwe.”

En: Without weakening in his faith, he faced the fact that his body was as good as dead—since he was about a hundred years old—and that Sarah’s womb was also dead.
Ib: Ka ọọdịdị mgbe ọ darị mba na ntụkwasịobu o nworu na-agbayegi na ọ kahịtuworu. Ọ dịzuru ihu ahọ ise nke na ike adịkọsịdịgị a. Sera nyee ye kahịtuwokoru nke na ọ dịsịgị nke ọ ga je-atụtakwakwa ime.

En: Yet he did not waver through unbelief regarding the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God,
Ib: Ka ọọdịkwarị mgbe obu meri e ụkpọrọ bayeri nkwam Chineke kweri e, kama ya o guzosiem ike na ntụkwasịobu o nworu, gaam na ihu na-anị Chineke otuto.

En: being fully persuaded that God had power to do what he had promised.
Ib: Maka na o docheri e ẹnya na Chineke nworu ikike imezu ihom o kweri e na nkwa.

En: This is why “it was credited to him as righteousness.”
Ib: Ọ bụ a meri “a gụụrụ a ya na ọ bụ ụmara-ọma.”

En: The words “it was credited to him” were written not for him alone,
Ib: Mgbem e deri na, “a gụụrụ a ya” ọ bụdịgịnwa maka yaanịa,

En: but also for us, to whom God will credit righteousness—for us who believe in him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.
Ib: kama ọ bụkọ maa ayịande, bụ nde Chineke je-agụkọ na nde ụmara-ọma, bụ nde nworu ntụkwasịobu na yaoni bụ Chineke, onye meri Onyenwoayị Jisọs Karaịs hi na ọnwụ pavuru.

En: He was delivered over to death for our sins and was raised to life for our justification.
Ib: Chineke nịrị Jisọs na ọnwụa ọnwụ maka ihe ọjọọ aayị, mie ya o hi na ọnwụ pavuru ma ayị bụrụ nde a nabatarị na ihu Chineke.

En: Therefore, since we have been justified through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
Ib: Ibe e jiworu okwukwe me ayị bụrụ nde a nabataworu na ihu Chineke, ayịa Chineke dịzuu na udo hite na ẹka Jisọs Karaịs Onyenwoayị.

En: through whom we have gained access by faith into this grace in which we now stand. And we boast in the hope of the glory of God.
Ib: Ayị gawokoru ẹka a nata ẹwụọma Chineke bụ nke ayị jiri dị ndụ ẹɦụọdị. Ayị na-anwụrị ọnwụ maka olile-ẹnya ayị nworu iso kete oke na ebube Chineke.

En: Not only so, but we also glory in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance;
Ib: Ka ọọbụnwa ya ọmụ, obu dịkọ ayị ụtọ na ime ahụhụ ayị nọ na ya, maka na ayị maarị na ayị tadụa ya ahụhụa na o weteri ayị ịta lịlịlị,

En: perseverance, character; and character, hope.
Ib: mgbe ayị nworu ike ịta lịlịlị, na ayị amụta ime ụmara dị ma, na ya ụmara-ọmam eweteri ayị olile-ẹnya.

En: And hope does not put us to shame, because God’s love has been poured out into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us.
Ib: Ya olile-ẹnyam amagị agarịfụkwanụ ayị, maka na Chineke eweworu ịhụnẹnya a wụjue ayị na obu, hite na Maa Nsọ ọ nịrị ayị.

En: You see, at just the right time, when we were still powerless, Christ died for the ungodly.
Ib: Na mgbe ayị eenwodigi ike ime ihe ọọbụla, Karaịs bịarị bịa-anwụhụrụ nde ihe ọjọọ, aamagị Chineke.

En: Very rarely will anyone die for a righteous person, though for a good person someone might possibly dare to die.
Ib: Ọ nyịrị anyị madụ ikwe bịa bịa-anwụhụchieri onye ụmara-ọma. Madụ nwokwenururi ike ịsị na ọ nwụhụchieri ezibe madụ.

En: But God demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
Ib: Ọbụ na nke Chineke garị gusi nke ọ garị hụ ayị na ẹnya bụ: Na mgbe ayị ka abụrụrị nde ihe ọjọọ, Karaịs bịarị bịa-anwụhụchieri ayị ọnwụ.

En: Since we have now been justified by his blood, how much more shall we be saved from God’s wrath through him!
Ib: Ibe ọ bụ na ayị abụworu nde a nabatarị na ihu Chineke maka mee Jisọs, Karaịs je-azọfụtarịrị ayị na iwe-ọkụ Chineke.

En: For if, while we were God’s enemies, we were reconciled to him through the death of his Son, how much more, having been reconciled, shall we
Ib: Maka na mgbe ayịa Chineke ka abụrụ nde-iro, na ọ bịarị bịa-ekpie udo na etiti ayịa ya hite na ọnwụ Ọkpara a, ọ bụa meri ya Ọkpara am je-azọfụtarịrị ayị hite na ndụ a.

En: Not only is this so, but we also boast in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.
Ib: Ka ọọbụnwa na ọ dị ya ẹɦụm, ayị na-anwụrịkọ ọnwụ maka nke ayịa Chineke dịzu na udo hite na ẹka Onyenwoayị bụ Karaịs Jisọs, onye kpeworu udo na etiti ayịa Chineke.

En: Death Through Adam, Life Through Christ
Ib: Ọnwụ Na Ẹka Adam Ndụ Na Ẹka Karaịs

En: Therefore, just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, and in this way death came to all people, because all sinned—
Ib: Ọ bụa meri, dịka nke omume ihe ọjọọ garị ẹka onye aanị gabata na ụwa, ọnwụ ga omume ihe ọjọọ gabata, ya ọ bụrụ nke ọnwụ garị rubetue ihe ọọbụla bụ madụ, maka na madụ oohu bụ nde ihe ọjọọ na ihu Chineke.

En: To be sure, sin was in the world before the law was given, but sin is not charged against anyone’s account where there is no law.
Ib: Maka na mgbem Chineke aaka agagị ẹka Mosisi nị iwu, ihe ọjọọ dịwozuru na ụwa. Ọbụ na ọ dịgị onye je-agụkọta ihe ọjọọ ma ya ọ dịgị iwu sị na-emesi ihe dị ya ẹɦụm.

En: Nevertheless, death reigned from the time of Adam to the time of Moses, even over those who did not sin by breaking a command, as did Adam, who is a pattern of the one to come.
Ib: Ọbụ na ọnwụ nọkwarịrị na-egbu ụmụ madụ hite na mgbe Adam rue na mgbe Mosisi. Ma ọ bụkọhaagị nde aadịdịgị ihe ọjọọ wo meri ka Adam. Adam dịrị ka ya Onyem bụ Karaịs Jisọs ka-abịatajeri na ọdị-na-ihu.

En: But the gift is not like the trespass. For if the many died by the trespass of the one man, how much more did God’s grace and the gift that came by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, overflow to the many!
